_meta.description: FICTIONAL demo utility for testing diagnostic Business Plan Studio (Option B). All names, people and figures are invented.

utility.name: Valle Verde Water and Sanitation Company (DEMO)

scenarios.name: Baseline
scenarios.description: Business as usual: no new actions; tariffs +4%/yr nominal; maintenance CAPEX USD 1.5 M/yr.

scenarios.name: Improvement
scenarios.description: Full program of 7 actions (USD 18.7 M CAPEX), World Bank loan USD 14 M, same tariff path as Baseline.

profile.history: Created in 1987 as a municipal decentralized public company; corporatized in 2009 under the national water services law.
profile.governance: Board of 7 members chaired by the mayor; CEO appointed by the board; economic regulation by the national regulator.

module2.mission: Provide safe, reliable and affordable water and sanitation services to every household in Valle Verde, every day.
module2.vision: By 2035, to be the most efficient and trusted water utility in the region, with universal access and full cost recovery.

objectives.title: Reduce non-revenue water
objectives.smart: Reduce NRW from 43.0% (2025) to 33.0% by December 2030 through district metered areas, pressure management and replacement of 60,000 meters.

objectives.title: Improve commercial efficiency
objectives.smart: Raise the collection ratio from 83% (2025) to 93% by December 2030 by implementing a new commercial and billing system by June 2027 and a collection campaign.

objectives.title: Strengthen financial sustainability
objectives.smart: Increase EBITDA margin from 18.2% (2025) to at least 23% by 2030 and keep DSCR above 1.5 every year, including a production cost per m3 8% below the Baseline from 2028.

objectives.title: Expand access to services
objectives.smart: Add 8,000 water connections in peri-urban areas (2027-2030) and 3,000 sewer connections after rehabilitating the North WWTP by 2029.

objectives.title: Develop human talent
objectives.smart: Train 100% of 64 supervisors and 120 technical staff in leadership and asset management by December 2028.

demographics.implications: Households grow faster than population (smaller households), so connections grow ~2.3%/yr; peri-urban growth to the south requires network expansion.

enablement_environment.assessment: National water law sets cost-recovery principle; municipal politics delay decisions.
Weak coordination between municipality and region on peri-urban expansion.
Tariff indexation allowed up to inflation; access to national fund and IFI loans with sovereign guarantee.
Quality standards enforced; performance benchmarking published yearly.

weaknesses: Collection ratio of 83% and legacy billing system
High energy cost at pumping stations
opportunities: World Bank financing for NRW and sanitation
Tariff indexation to inflation allowed by regulator
threats: Drought periods reducing raw water availability

strengths: Committed management team after previous improvement program
weaknesses: NRW of 43% with 34% of connections unmetered

previous_improvement_program.impact: Collection rose 1.5 points in 100 days after a door-to-door campaign in two districts; 1,200 illegal connections regularized.

charters.mission: Cut physical losses by sectorizing the network into 24 district metered areas with pressure control.
charters.scope: Design and install 24 DMAs, 40 pressure-reducing valves, flow meters and SCADA links.

charters.mission: Meter every connection accurately to bill real consumption.
charters.scope: Procure and install 60,000 class C meters; update customer database.

charters.mission: Replace the 2004 billing system and raise collection.
charters.scope: CIS implementation, data migration, mobile collection, campaign.

charters.mission: Restore treatment capacity to enable 3,000 new sewer connections.

module5.note: Actuals 2022-2025 identical in both scenarios. Expenses positive. Depreciation includes incremental depreciation = cumulative action CAPEX / 25 years.

kpis.name: Collection ratio
kpis.formula: collections from customers / billed customer revenue

kpis.name: Water coverage
kpis.formula: population served with water / population in service area

module8.executive_summary: Valle Verde (fictional) serves about 487,000 people with water (89% coverage) and 370,000 with sewerage. NRW of 43% and collection of 83% limit its finances. The plan invests USD 18.7 M in seven actions (2026-2030), financed with a USD 14 M World Bank loan and own funds. By 2030 it targets NRW 33%, collection 93%, EBITDA margin about 24% and DSCR above 1.5, while lowering the tariff needed for cost recovery compared with the Baseline.
